item.title: Russia Says It Will Stick To New Start’s Nuclear Arms Limits As Long As US Does
item.description: By VLADIMIR ISACHENKOV Associated Press MOSCOW (AP) — Moscow will observe the limits of the last nuclear arms pact with the United States that expired last week as long as it sees that Washington is doing the same, Russia’s top diplomat said Wednesday. item.title: A 130,000 Surge In US Hiring Last Month Is A Stark Contrast To The Drastic Job Cuts Of 2025
item.description: By PAUL WISEMAN AP Economics Writer WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. employers added a surprisingly strong 130,000 jobs last month, but government revisions cut 2024-2025 U.S. payrolls by hundreds of thousands. The unemployment rate fell to 4.3%, the Labor Department said Wednesday. item.title: Teen Shooting Scare
item.description: The cops in suburban Houston are looking for three suspects after a teenage boy was shot during a social media meetup. The Precinct-four constable’s office says the 16-year-old was trying to sell vape pens at his apartment complex in the town of Spring Tuesday night when gunfire erupted, sending him to the hospital with non life threatening injuries. The suspects ran to a waiting car and took off.

item.title: Redistricting House Maps
item.description: The head of the Texas Republican Party wants to re-draw state house districts to make them more GOP-friendly. But even his fellow republicans say that’s a pipe dream. Texas GOP Strategist Bill Miller says redistricting is controversial on both sides. And, for republicans, he says they have the numbers to get things done. Last session, the legislature passed around four-dozen “priority” bills.

item.title: Gender Surgery Suit
item.description: An anti-transgender activist, who had her surgery reversed, wants to sue the psychiatrist and surgeons involved in her medical transition. The case of Soren Aldaco, today, went before the Supreme Court of Texas. Her attorney, John Ramer, says what happened to his client was “medical scandal.”. Aldaco has been trying to argue that the state’s two year deadline for medical malpractice cases should not apply when they involve gender-modification.
